# Sourdough starter guide

A new starter is made from equal weights of flour and water. For the first
week it is fed once a day, discarding half before each feeding so that the
culture does not outgrow its jar.

A healthy starter doubles in size within six hours of feeding at room
temperature. If it smells of nail polish remover it is hungry and should be fed
more often. A thin grey liquid on top is called hooch and can be stirred back
in.

Whole rye flour speeds up fermentation because it carries more wild yeast and
nutrients. Many bakers keep a small rye starter and build the dough from it the
night before baking.

Dough is baked in a preheated Dutch oven at 240 degrees Celsius. The lid stays
on for the first twenty minutes to trap steam, then comes off so that the crust
can brown.
